title: Bahasa Inggris Fase E · Bertingkat
subject: inggris
description: Perfect tenses, relative clauses, conditionals, gerunds, an expository text on mangroves, sources, and logical fallacies.
topic: Perfect tenses, relative clauses, conditionals, gerunds, expository reading, argument (English Fase E)

items.explanation: Present perfect: have/has + past participle. Finish → finished.

items.stem: A word with a similar meaning to significant is ....
items.explanation: Significant means important or large enough to be noticed.

items.stem: The main purpose of a report text is to ....
options: describe things in general, based on facts
tell a story with a problem
items.explanation: A report text describes a class of things in general, for example "Mangroves" or "Volcanoes", using facts.

items.stem: The scientist ___ discovered the vaccine received an award.
items.explanation: Use who for people in a relative clause. Use which for things and where for places.

items.stem: If I ___ a bird, I would fly over the sea.
items.explanation: Second conditional for imaginary situations: if + past (were for all subjects), would + verb.

items.stem: She enjoys ___ novels in her free time.
items.explanation: After enjoy, use a gerund (verb + -ing): enjoys reading.

items.stem:
Read the text.
Mangrove forests grow along tropical coasts. Their roots slow down waves and hold mud in place, so they protect the coast from erosion. Mangroves also store large amounts of carbon in their soil. However, many mangrove areas have been cleared for fish ponds and new buildings.
What is the main idea of the text?
options: Mangroves are useful, but they are under threat.
Fish ponds are better than forests.
Carbon is dangerous for the soil.
items.explanation: Most of the text explains how mangroves help (protection, carbon storage). The last sentence, starting with "However", shows the threat. The main idea combines both.

hints: What does most of the text talk about? What changes after 'However'?

items.stem: In the text, the word However signals ....
items.explanation: "However" introduces an idea that contrasts with the one before: mangroves are useful, however they are being cleared.

items.stem: "Mangroves also store large amounts of carbon in their soil." Here, store means ....
items.explanation: In this sentence store is a verb meaning to keep something for a long time, not a noun meaning a shop.

items.stem: You want reliable data on air quality in Indonesian cities. Which source is the most reliable?
options: A monitoring report from a government agency or university that explains its methods
items.explanation: A reliable source is accountable, explains how the data was collected, and does not profit from the conclusion. An advertisement wants to sell, and an anonymous post cannot be checked.

items.stem: "Everyone uses plastic straws, so they can't be harmful." Why is this argument weak?
options: Popularity does not prove that something is harmless.
items.explanation: This is a bandwagon fallacy: something is not true or safe just because many people do it.

items.stem: Choose the best concluding sentence for a paragraph about the benefits of solar energy in Indonesia.
options: Therefore, solar energy is a promising option for a sunny country like Indonesia.
Solar panels are blue and black.
items.explanation: A concluding sentence sums up the paragraph and links back to its topic. Only the first option does that.
